summary: Implemented a strengthened multi-subject interpretability smoke test for the KUL LOSO AAD-Conformer by adding quantitative PSD-based frequency validation, stricter baseline verification, and a structural checkpoint sanity check. The review failed because the implementation still overclaimed executable verification of the preprocessing pipeline and checkpoint compatibility beyond what was actually validated.
lessons: Restrict methodological claims to behaviors that are directly demonstrated by executable code.
Differentiate validation of cached signal properties from validation of the preprocessing implementation that produced those signals.
Quantitative perturbation checks provide stronger evidence than qualitative visualizations but do not by themselves verify upstream preprocessing.
Treat structural checkpoint inspections as sanity checks unless dataset identity, preprocessing version, architecture metadata, and provenance are explicitly validated.
Do not describe checkpoint compatibility or provenance as verified when only parameter structure or successful loading has been checked.
Use baseline metric agreement as behavioral consistency validation rather than evidence of checkpoint provenance.
Clearly distinguish smoke-test characterization from comprehensive scientific validation in documentation and reporting.
Heuristic validation thresholds should not be presented as specification-derived acceptance criteria unless they are justified by the preprocessing design.
task: Run 3.1 Frequency Pipeline Verification and Multi-Subject Smoke Test
